name: 欧美幻想叙事卡牌插画-更保守
suffix:
VISUAL LANGUAGE: polished Western fantasy game narrative illustration with animation-film energy; funny, bold, slightly odd but appealing caricature; designed stylized proportions with strong silhouette rhythm and varied volume scale; large expressive hands; graphic eyes; directional noses, chins and smiles; hair, fabric, plants and props grouped into a few strong flowing shapes. Every person, creature and object has toy-like, puppet-like shape appeal.

ANATOMY BOUNDARY: preserve believable skeletal construction, joint orientation, neck-to-shoulder connection, ribcage-to-pelvis relationship, weight-bearing logic, and recognizable hand and foot structure. Apply exaggeration primarily to overall proportion, silhouette rhythm, shape contrast and volume scale—not through arbitrary neck or limb elongation, broken joint direction, collapsed wrists or ankles, twisted feet, or impossible load distribution. Hands and feet may be enlarged and simplified, but their attachment, gesture and structural direction must remain coherent. Foreshortening may strongly enlarge nearer forms while preserving continuous limb construction and readable joints.

COLOR SYSTEM: the hue palette must arise from the theme, but never become conservative naturalistic color. Use bright, clean, animation-illustration saturation, a clearly dominant vivid color family, a strong structural contrast and one tiny near-maximum-chroma focal accent. Keep shadows chromatic and full of hue, not gray or black. Put the brightest and most saturated color near the story focal point and taper saturation and contrast toward the edges. Make the whole image feel luminous, translucent and color-rich even when the scene is cloudy, underwater or indoors. Do not fall back on a fixed palette formula.

SURFACE AND BRUSH CONTROL: create sculptural volume with broad, complete, clean color masses and long smooth gradients. Each major form should read through only a few large light-and-shadow shapes. Brush direction follows the full form and silhouette. Do not fragment surfaces into many short strokes, tiny planes, noisy highlights or microtexture. Group hair into a few large locks; keep only major cloth folds; use continuous smooth skin transitions; simplify fur, foliage, weaving, masonry and metal into broad readable masses. Indicate material with a few designed highlights, edges and color shifts rather than literal texture. Highly polished and refined, but not busy. Precision comes from clean large shapes, controlled gradients and a few crisp focal details.

No black outlines. Most edges are soft, lost or merged into shared environmental light; crisp edges only around eyes, mouth, hands, core prop and a few silhouette intersections. Use an off-center asymmetric composition, tilted perspective, controlled near-to-far scale exaggeration that preserves joint logic and limb continuity, cropping, foreground occlusion, overlapping forms and a sweeping curve. Include a humorous secondary action where appropriate. Avoid conventional glamour faces, centered front-facing poses, symmetrical catalog presentation, generic epic realism, muted realism, dense ornament, visible bristle noise, repetitive small texture, uniform sharpness, anatomically broken joints, twisted necks, malformed hands or feet, impossible weight-bearing, text, logo, border and watermark.
